question: A primary radial nerve palsy developing immediately after a closed mid-shaft humeral shaft fracture is a neurapraxia in the vast majority of cases, and spontaneous recovery occurs in approximately 70–90% of patients within 3–4 months.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The overwhelming majority of immediate post-fracture radial nerve palsies in closed injuries are neurapraxias. Expectant management with serial clinical and electrophysiological monitoring is appropriate; spontaneous recovery occurs in 70–90% within 3–4 months.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Most primary radial nerve palsies after closed humeral shaft fractures are neurapraxias caused by traction or contusion in the radial groove. The 'rule of 70–90%' applies — watch-and-wait with nerve conduction studies at 6–8 weeks is the standard approach. Surgery is reserved for failure to recover or confirmed laceration.
